blocks.text: A multi-column join missing one column is a data leak, not a slow query. Use INNER JOIN only when a missing match makes the row irrelevant to the question.

blocks.text: A WHERE on either table's columns silently degrades FULL to an inner-ish join. Filter in the ON clause or wrap the side in a subquery. Engines pick hash or merge here — nested loop cannot emit unmatched right rows.

caption.text: Most SQL bugs don't crash — they quietly return the wrong number. A WHERE clause in the wrong place turns your LEFT JOIN into an INNER one, a many:many join triples your revenue total, and one NULL inside a NOT IN subquery wipes the whole result set. 10 pages: every join type, every set operator, the three execution algorithms, and the exact mistakes that corrupt results without ever throwing an error.
